title: Financing climate resilience: 3 ways cities are pivoting as federal funding dwindles
summary: Local leaders are turning to layered programs, new financing tools and deeper community engagement to prepare for extreme weather.

title: Fair housing construction accessibility complaints now have a deadline, HUD says
summary: Accessibility claims related to multifamily building design and construction must be filed within one year of the initial certificate of occupancy, the new guidance says.

title: AI oversight still lacking in NYC despite city progress: state audit
summary: The city has “partially implemented” state recommendations to bolster AI governance, the New York State comptroller found.

title: Food waste collection for multifamily housing expands in D.C.
summary: The city's smart bin program will add another 20 collection locations. It’s part of an effort to increase multifamily composting efforts to meet D.C.'s zero waste goal to divert 80% of waste by 2040.

title: Ridership up, crime down on LA Metro transit system
summary: New transit openings, major events and a drop in crime helped bring riders back, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority said.

title: Local government is fragmented. Here’s how AI is helping residents navigate it.
summary: Virtual assistants are searching across agencies and data sets to deliver answers, maps and resources through simple, conversational questions.

title: New York’s congestion pricing program has not affected air quality, study finds
summary: The study addresses fears that the program would increase pollution if drivers tried to avoid the toll.

title: For affordable housing fund, Cleveland embraces private partnerships
summary: The city launched a fund to build up to 3,000 affordable housing units using leftover American Rescue Plan Act money.

title: Chicago-area transit agencies start operating under new regional authority
summary: The state restructured the six-county Northern Illinois transit system last year and provided $1.5 billion for transportation and transit-oriented development.

title: Water cybersecurity gets federal boost in 10 cities and Texas
summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency is putting nearly $12 million behind water-system cybersecurity and resilience as the White House connects Texas utilities with free cyber defense resources.
